comments.body:
FWIW I'm able to work around this by replacing
```python
def raises(_):
    raise ValueError("error message goes here")
```
with something akin to:
```python
def raises(_):
    print("error message goes here")
    sys.exit()
```
This crashes the whole runtime rather than gracefully raising an exception (`terminate called after throwing an instance of 'pybind11::error_already_set' ... Aborted (core dumped)`) but that's still better than proceeding with a wrong computation.
Closing as `host_callback` is deprecated in favour of `jax.pure_callback` (which does raise exceptions on both CPU and GPU).

issue.body:
```python
import jax
import jax.experimental.host_callback as hcb

def raises(_):
    raise ValueError

@jax.jit
def f():
    hcb.call(raises, None)

try:
    f()
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e))
```
(JAX version 0.2.27)

This prints `<class 'ValueError'>` on CPU (as expected) but instead just prints a traceback to stdout/stderr on GPU. (i.e. no exception is raised.)

To be clear I'm aware of the whole "XLA doesn't support errors" problem. My assumption based on the CPU behaviour was that JAX worked around this (when errors are raised in `hcb.call`) by waiting for the XLA computation to complete, and then raising the appropriate error. Either that assumption was wrong, or it would seem that the GPU behaviour is wrong.

I appreciate this is pretty experimental / edge-case behaviour. FWIW my use-case is that I'd like to check the arguments passed to library functions, and raise an error if they're wrong.
issue.title: `jax.experimental.host_callback.call` has different behaviour on CPU vs GPU, for exceptions

issue.body: When jit-compiling on the GPU: errors are currently only printed to stdout/stderr rather than properly raising. See https://github.com/google/jax/issues/9457, including the bare-bones of a possible workaround. In practice it'd be better to format the traceback appropriately, using the `traceback` module; see also https://github.com/google/jax/blob/7a6986c4c8fd8469bae36306efb0417b0a2f6d8c/jax/_src/traceback_util.py for inspiration.

issue.body:
I recently required a fast i.e. jit-able version of SciPy's RegularGridInterpolator and adapted the original code in SciPy to work with JAX, see [this RegularGridInterpolator gist](https://gist.github.com/Edenhofer/f248f0de5a1dce54a246375d53345bc5). Is there any interest in putting a tidier version of this into JAX? If so I would be more than happy to file a merge request.

If there is interest in having this in JAX what should be done about sanity checks within the code. Code that performs such checks needs to run during the initialization of the class. However, JAX's omni-staging staging might disallow probing the truthfullness of any such checks if jitted. Should code blocks such as the following thus simply remain in numpy?
```python
if not np.all(np.diff(p) > 0.):
    raise ValueError(f"the points in dimension {i} must be strictly ascending")
```

issue.body:
Summary: if enough weights/probabilities are zero such that sampling w/o replacement leads to too few possibilities to sample, jax should raise an error.
Simple case: 
```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

prob = jnp.zeros(10)
prob = prob.at[9].set(1)
jax.random.choice(jax.random.PRNGKey(5), jnp.arange(10), shape=(5,), replace=False, p=prob)
# DeviceArray([9, 0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=int32)
```
Numpy raises a 
```
ValueError: Fewer non-zero entries in p than size
```
with equivalent code.

Fix: 
https://github.com/google/jax/blob/main/jax/_src/random.py#L493
Here, do a check that the number of nonzero entries is >= desired number of entries.

issue.body:
In Flax, Batch Normalization is a bit finicky since each call to `apply` requires marking `batch_stats` as mutable and updating the `batch_stats` afterward.

```python
bn = flax.linen.BatchNorm(use_running_average=True)

x = jnp.arange(24).reshape(3, 6)

vars = bn.init(random.PRNGKey(0), x)

# Mark the batch stats as mutable so we can update them in the variable dictionary
x_normed, mutated_vars = bn.apply(vars, x, mutable=['batch_stats'])

vars = {**vars, **mutated_vars}  # Update the variables with our diff

x_normed2, mutated_vars2 = bn.apply(vars, x, mutable=['batch_stats'])
```

How could this be implemented as a Module in Equinox? I'm happy to submit an implementation given some guidance.
